event.label: c. 1475–1480 (Reign of Edward IV) — Earliest Ancestors Born: Edmond Lushe (Melbury Abbas) & William Squyer (Buckland Newton)
event.desc: Pushes our family lifespan back ~551 years to the reign of King Edward IV: by Spring 1539, Edmond Lushe was already past the age-60 active-marching limit while owning a full suit of steel armour in East Melbury, alongside William Squyer (born c. 1475–1495), who already had a tax-paying son over age 16 in 1524.
event.note: [TNA E 36/17, Spring 1539, p. 95, Melbary] Edm Lushe — NA [is no able man, aged 60+], has pr al.rivets. [TNA E 179/103/119–120, 1524, Knolle] William Squyer — G 5; Thomas Squyer [aged 16+] — G 1.
King Henry VIII's February 1539 muster enrolled able-bodied men aged 16 to 60; being marked 'NA' while owning expensive German plate armour proves Edmond was over age 60 rather than poor.

event.label: c. 1500–1508 (Reign of Henry VII) — Birth of Thomas Squyer / Squier of Bookham Farm (Buckland Newton)
event.desc: Because Thomas Squyer had reached the age-16+ tax threshold in 1524 right beneath his father William Squyer, we know he was born c. 1500–1508 under King Henry VII. He farmed at Bookham into his seventies and was buried there on February 15, 1579/80.
event.note: [TNA E 179/103/119, 1524, Hundredum de Bucklond — Knolle] William Squyer — G 5 | Thomas Squyer — G 1 [statutory 16+ threshold]. [PE/BCN/RE 1/1 f. 19r, 15 Feb 1579/80] sepultus fuit Thomas Squier de Bewcombe.
Under the 1523 tax law, young unmarried sons aged 16+ earning wages were listed at the £1 entry rate directly beneath their fathers.

event.label: October 1523 — Edmond Lushe Taxed on £40 by King Henry VIII — Richest 1.7% of All Dorset
event.desc: Our oldest exact-dated written family record (503 years ago). When King Henry VIII demanded an advance war loan from only the wealthiest households worth £40 or more, Edmond Lushe was one of just 7 farmers in Sixpenny Handley Hundred—and in the richest 1.7% (143 out of 8,369) of all taxpayers in Dorset.
event.note: [TNA E 179/103/116 & 128, Oct. 1523 Anticipation, Sixpenny Handley Hundred, Stoate 1982 p. 222] Walter Kyng £60; Henry Kyng £50; Robert Pulvertoft sen. £50; Thomas Pety £50; Edmond Lushe £40 (tax 40s.); William Were £40; Alice Ridoute wid. £40. [Ashmore] Richard Burdon £60. [Brockhampton] Thomas Lock G 50.
Tudor tax assessors valued livestock and grain conservatively, meaning a £40 tax rating reflected roughly £120–£160 in real sheep flocks, oxen, harvested grain, and silver coin.

event.label: 1524 & January 6, 1525 — William & Thomas Squyer Taxed Together in Knoll; Edmond Lusshe in East Melbury & Robert Akerman on Coast
event.desc: More than a decade before English church registers even began in 1538, King Henry VIII's village tax rolls capture all three of our English ancestral lines at once: father and son William & Thomas Squyer at Knoll/Bookham, Edmond Lusshe as second-richest farmer in East Melbury, and Robert Akerman near Bridport.
event.note: [E 179/103/119–120, Knoll, p. 162] William Squyer G 5; Thomas Squyer G 1; John Robertes G 2; Robert Roberdes G 5. [Alton Pancras, p. 199] Robert Squyer G 2. [E 179/103/122, Shipton Gorge, p. 55] Robert Akerman G 10. [E 179/103/121, Est Melbury, Jan. 6, 1525, p. 139] Robert Kyng G 30; Edmond Lusshe G 20; West Melbury: Thomas Rydoutte G 1; Est Compton: John Burden G 10.
Checking the entire county tax roll separates our ancestors from unrelated look-alike names in distant Dorset towns like Wareham and Maiden Newton.

event.label: 1528–1529 — Melbury Abbas Manor Court Roll Lists Lush & Chyckeford Farm Holdings
event.desc: Records the Lush family's leased farm in Melbury Abbas right beside the Chyckeford family—the exact in-laws later named in John Lusshe's 1572 will—while the 1523–1545 tax rolls confirm Edmond Lusshe as the head of that farm.
event.note: [Wiltshire & Swindon History Centre Ref: 2667/13/403, 20 Hen. VIII, 1528–1529] Curia Manerii de Melbury Abbatisse — Lush & Chyckeford customary copyhold tenements.
Surrounding 1523, 1525, 1539, 1542, and 1545 Crown rolls confirm Edmond Lusshe's first name without needing to handle the fragile 1528 parchment.

event.label: April 10 & May 15, 1539 — 1539 Invasion Musters: Thomas Squyer (Billhook), Akerman Longbowmen & Edmond Lushe (Steel Plate Armour)
event.desc: When King Henry VIII called out every village to prepare against a French invasion, Thomas Squyer marched in Knoll carrying his own billhook beside neighbours Roberds and Farvell, Akerman archers mustered with longbows near Bridport, and elder Edmond Lushe supplied riveted German steel plate armour in Melbury Abbas.
event.note: [E 36/29, May 15, 1539, Knowlle, p. 36] B Tho Squyer — bill; Rob Roberds — bill, splints; Rob Farvell — poleaxe. [SP 2/S, Liberty of Alton, p. 50] Rob Squyer — harness for man, bow, sh.arr; B Jn Squyer — bow, 4 arr. [E 36/29, Apr. 10, 1539, p. 8] Jn Akerman — bow, sh.arr; Ste Akerman — bill; A Hen Akerman — AA, bow, sh.arr. [E 36/17, Melbary, p. 95] Edm Lushe — NA, has pr al.rivets.
Tudor muster codes ('A' for archer, 'B' for billman, and 'NA' for men past age 60) give us exact age brackets before birth certificates existed.

event.label: 1542 — Teenage John Lusshe Turns 16+ and Joins His Father Edmond Lushe on the 1542 Muster Roll
event.desc: Too young (under 16) to appear in 1539, John Lusshe (Gen 15) steps onto the 1542 military roll alongside his elderly father Edmond Lushe—pinpointing John's birth to c. 1523–1526—while relative Walter Lusshe appears next door in Fontmell.
event.note: [TNA E 101/61/36, 1542 King's Remembrancer Muster, Comton Abbas & West Melberys, Stoate 1978 p. 96] Edm Lushe — NA, has pr al.rivets ... Jn Lusshe [ableman, newly aged 16+]. [Fonntmell, p. 94] Walt Lusshe.
Seeing elder Edm Lushe and newly adult Jn Lusshe together on the 1542 roll cleanly links Generation 16 to Generation 15.

event.label: 1535 – September 1544 — King Henry VIII Closes Shaftesbury Abbey & Sells Melbury, Compton & Fontmell Together to Sir Thomas Arundell
event.desc: Solves a 200-year puzzle in our Lush tree: before March 1539, Edmond Lusshe leased his farm from England's richest nunnery, Shaftesbury Abbey (with no local squire living in the village, Edmond's personal farming wealth rivaled the entire manor's fixed rent roll!). In September 1544, King Henry VIII sold Melbury Abbas, Compton Abbas, and Fontmell in one bundle to Sir Thomas Arundell of Wardour—explaining why Edmond's descendants moved freely across those exact three villages for the next two centuries.
event.note: [Valor Ecclesiasticus, 1535, Vol. I] Shaftesbury Abbey: gross £1,329 1s. 3d.; clear net £1,166 8s. 9d. [L&P Hen. VIII, Vol. 17, 1541–42, pp. 690–705] Core grain-rent manors: Melbury, Fountmell, Hanleigh, Iwern. [Letters Patent, Sept. 1544, 36 Hen. VIII; L&P Vol. 19 Pt. 2, pp. 158–197] Crown sale (£2,609 11s. 1d.; Dorset clear yearly rent £58) to Sir Thomas Arundell: Manors of Melbury Abbatisse & Compton Abbatisse, with advowson of Fontmell.
Matching the 1535 abbey valuation, 1541–42 Crown accounts, and September 1544 royal charter proves all three Lush parishes belonged to one unified estate.

event.label: 1543–1545 — Thomas Squyer Heads the Knoll Farm Alone (1543–44); Edmond & Young John Lusshe Both Taxed in 1545
event.desc: By 1543–44, Thomas Squyer had taken over his father William's farm in Knoll, while in 1545 elderly Edmond Lusshe (still one of the four richest men in Melbury Abbas) appears in the same year his young son John Lusshe pays his first tax.
event.note: [E 179/104/151–152, Knoll, 1543–44, p. 162] Thomas Squyer — G 1½ (30s.; tithing sum 4s. 7½d.); William Locke G 4; Robert Roberdes G 3. [Alton, p. 199] Robert Squyer G 5; John Squyer G 1. [E 179/104/156, June 1545 Melbury Anticipation, p. 141] Edmond Lusshe — G 13. [E 179/104/154, Cann/Melbury, p. 142] John Lusshe — G 1; Thomas Rideoute G 4. [Bothenhampton, p. 54] Henry Akerman — G 4.
Adding up the exact pennies and halfpennies of the 1544 Knoll village total (4s. 7½d.) proves Thomas Squyer's 30-shilling ('G 1½') assessment to the halfpenny.

event.label: 1558–1576 — Tudor Wills in Neighbouring Alton Pancras (Nicholas Locke 1558, John Squire 1565 & Robert Squire 1576)
event.desc: Proves that branches of our Squire and Locke families were already farming across the 1.5-mile hedge in Alton Pancras in the 1500s—so when John and Roger Squire moved there from Bookham in 1678, they were returning to an old family village.
event.note: [Dean of Salisbury Peculiar Will Registers, Series I, BRS Vol. 53] 1558: Nicholas Locke, Alton Pancras (Vol. 1, p. 89) | 1565: John Squire, Alton Pancras, A. & W. (Vol. 1, pp. 65, 68) | 1576: Robert Squire / Squier, Alton Pancras (Vol. 3, p. 83).
Because Alton Pancras answered to the Dean of Salisbury rather than the local Dorset court, its 1500s will registers survived fires and wartime bombings.

event.label: March–August 1569 — Thomas Lawrens Sr. Supplies Armour in Merriott (Somerset) & Richard Akerman Musters as Bridport Archer
event.desc: Introduces our Somerset ancestors—prosperous farmer Thomas Lawrens Sr. (supplying steel plate armour) and archer Peter Langdon in Merriott—alongside archer Richard Akerman in Bridport.
event.note: [SRS Vol. XX, 1569 Merriott Tithing, pp. 28–30] Armour: Florence Pytt wid. [PCC PROB 11/51/267, June 28, 1569], Thomas Lawrens Sr. ... furnish 1 almain rivet; Archer: Peter Langdon. [TNA SP 12/56, Birteporte, p. 143] A Ric Akerman; [Bovehinton & Lodres, p. 148] B Jn Akerman.
Only a small quota of fit men aged 16–60 were picked in 1569, explaining why ailing John Lusshe (who died in 1572) and his young son William were not required to march.

event.label: April 14 or 22, 1572 — 1572 Will of John Lusshe of Melbury Abbas Leaves £20 Cash to His Young Son William
event.desc: Proves directly that Gen 15 John Lusshe and his wife Alice were the parents of Gen 14 William Lusshe, leaving young William £20 in cash (a substantial Elizabethan fortune) safeguarded by uncles Robert Lusshe and John Chyckeford.
event.note: [Melbury Abbas Will, Apr. 14/22, 1572; calendared SDNQ 24:173, Dean & Chapter of Bristol] I John Lusshe of y^e p[ar]ishe of melbory ... geve and Bequeathe vnto my sonne william Lusshe xx^li [£20] of curra[n]t money of England ... when he is of lawfull age / Residue to Alice my wyffe executrixe / my twoe Brothers Rob[er]t Lusshe & John Chyckeford my overseers.
Careful reading of the old handwriting ('xx^li') confirms 20 pounds rather than 20 shillings, and filing at Bristol Cathedral saved this will from the 1731 Blandford fire.

event.label: Aug. 30, 1574 – Feb. 4, 1584/85 — Bookham Church Records: Johannes Squier Serves as Parish Churchwarden (1581–82) & Locke Marriage
event.desc: A page-by-page reading of Buckland Newton's surviving 1500s register captures three generations at Bookham ('Bewcombe'), records Edith Squier marrying neighbour Hugh Locke in 1578, and shows Gen 14 Johannes Squier elected Parish Churchwarden in 1581–82.
event.note: [DHC PE/BCN/RE 1/1] f. 10r (30 Aug 1574): baptizatus fuit Thomas Squier filius Johannis Squier de Bewcombe | f. 12v (18 Jan 1575/76): sepulta fuit Iuliana Squier | f. 16r (31 Jul 1578): matrimonium inter Hugonem Locke de Sharnhull et Editham Squier filiam Thome Squier de Bewcombe | f. 19r (15 Feb 1579/80): sepultus fuit Thomas Squier de Bewcombe | f. 23r (Mar 1581/82): Gilberto Duning, Johanne Squier } Gar[dianis] | f. 32 (4 Feb 1584/85): sepultus fuit Johannes Squier de Bewcombe.
Comparing letters side-by-side on the original page cleanly separates our surname Squier (hooked 'q') from a different village family named Spicer (closed 'p').

event.label: 1594 — William & Ellen Lushe Farm a 4-Load Estate in Fontmell Magna (Tax Roll, Court Suit & Arundell Roll)
event.desc: Twenty-two years after inheriting £20 in his father's 1572 will, grown-up William Lushe and his wife Ellen appear across three independent records holding a 4-load farm in Fontmell Magna right inside the Arundell estate.
event.note: [TNA E 179/105/253, 1594 Fontmell Tithing, p. 143] William Lushe — G 3; Robert Rydoute — G 4; Thomas Rydoute sen. — G 3. [TNA REQ 2/128/60, Wylde v Lushe] William Lushe and Ellen Lushe his wife, Manor of Fontmell. [Arundell Carriage Roll, SDNQ 34.351:353] William Lushe, 4 loads; Wylde, widow, 2 loads; Robert Rydowt, 6 loads. [Loders, p. 53] John Akerman — G 3.
Having a royal tax roll, a London court case (Wylde v Lushe), and the landlord's carriage list all name William Lushe beside widow Wylde and the Ridoutes leaves zero doubt.

event.label: September 20, 1598 — 24-Year-Old Thomas Squire Recorded Holding His Knoll Farm "By Copy" of the Manor Roll
event.desc: Four weeks before baptizing his first child at Bookham in October 1598, 24-year-old Thomas Squire is officially taxed as a copyhold landowner ('in copy L 1') beside lifelong neighbours William Lock and William Robertes.
event.note: [TNA E 179/105/271, Sept. 20, 1598, Buckland Newton Hundred — Knoll Tithing, Stoate 1982 p. 162] Thomas S[quire] — in copy L 1; William Lock — G 4; William Robertes — in copy L 1.
Even though the parchment edge is worn after 'Thomas S...', his Bookham baptisms starting 25 days later confirm no other 'Thomas S-' farmed in Knoll.

event.label: Mar. 7, 1600/01 – May 9, 1613 — Baptism of Thomas Squire Senior (March 1601), Kinsman Roger Squier & Burial of Mother Maria Squier
event.desc: Pinpoints Gen 12 Thomas Squire senior's baptism to March 7, 1600/01 (making him 41 when he signed the 1642 Loyalty Oath and nearly 77 when he died in 1678), names his mother Maria, and confirms the family name Roger Squier at Bookham.
event.note: [DHC PE/BCN/RE 1/1] f. 73v (10 Aug 1600): Aliciam Squier filiam Rogeri Squier defunct[i] de Bewcombe | f. 73r (7 Mar 1600/01): baptizatus fuit Thomas Squier filius Thome Squier de Bewcombe | f. 99 (9 May 1613): sepulta fuit Maria Squier uxor Thome Squier de Bewcombe.
Before 1752 England started the new year on March 25, so 'March 7, 1600/01' is March 7, 1601 in our modern calendar.

event.label: Sept. 2, 1621 & Mar. 1621/22 — Churchwarden Thomas Squire Signs His Own Name in the Parish Book (Introducing Modern "Squire" Spelling)
event.desc: Forty years after his father served as Parish Churchwarden, 47-year-old Thomas Squire held the same respected office and signed his own name clearly—introducing the modern '-ire' spelling—while his co-warden could only sign with an 'X'.
event.note: [DHC PE/BCN/RE 1/1, f. 123r, Sept. 2, 1621, Reading-in of Henricus Allane, B.D.] Subscribed: Thomas Squire [confident autograph] & Robert [X] Witt } Churchwardens; John Roberts [witness]. [f. 124r, Mar. 1621/22] Thoma Squire et Roberto Witt } Gard.
Seeing his actual handwritten signature proves the Bookham Squires were literate yeoman farmers before the English Civil War.

event.label: 1637 & Feb.–Mar. 1641/42 — 1641/42 Civil War Loyalty Oaths: John Lush Sr. & Jr. (Fontmell) and Thomas Squire (Buckland Newton)
event.desc: Right before the English Civil War broke out, every adult man over 18 had to sign a loyalty oath: John Lush Sr. and Jr. signed on William Lushe's Fontmell land beside their Burte in-laws, while Thomas Squire signed at Bookham beside his childhood Lock and Roberts neighbours.
event.note: [SHC DD\SP/1637/22] Inventory of Thomas Lawrence Jr., Merriott. [Dorset Protestation Returns, Feb.–Mar. 1641/42, Fry 1912] Funtmill Tything (p. 137): John Lush, se.; John Lush, ju.; Robert Burte; James Burte [Compton Abbas: 0 Lush males]. Brockhampton Tithing (Mar. 6, 1641/42): Richard Lock; Thomas Squire; William Roberts; Willi. Lock; Tho. Roberts [Alton Pancras: 0 Squire males].

Because three-lives manor farms could not pass to strangers without court records—and zero Lush men lived in Compton Abbas and zero Squires lived in Alton Pancras in 1642—this bridges the Civil War gap.

event.label: 1656–1667 — Somerset Lawrence–Langdon–Shore Weddings, 4-Fireplace Lush Farmhouse & 1667 Melbury–Compton Roll
event.desc: Unites our Somerset Lawrence, Langdon, and Shore families, shows a substantial 4-fireplace Lush farmhouse next to James Burt in 1664, and documents Melbury Abbas land expanding into neighbouring Compton Abbas in 1667.
event.note: [SHC DP/MER/2/1/1, Sept. 16, 1656] Civil marriage: John Lawrence & Joane Langdon (dau. of John Langdon). [Crewkerne PR, Aug. 19, 1657] William Lawrence ['Lareme'] & Sarah Shore. [1664 Hearth Tax, Meekings p. 24] William Lush — iiij [4 hearths]; James Burt — ij. [WSHC Ref: 413/162, 1667] Melbury Abbas & Compton manorial court roll.
Reading the original parish pages restores 'Joane Langdon' (cut off as 'Lang' in old indexes) and 'Lawrence' (spelled phonetically as 'Lareme').

event.label: Feb. 25, 1672/73 – Aug. 1676 — 1673 Melbury Will (£50 Dowry), Shared Compton Churchyard & Aug. 1676 Baptism of Edmund Lush
event.desc: Nicholas and Mary Lush baptize Gen 11 Edmund Lush in Compton Abbas in August 1676—reviving the first name of Gen 16 founder Edmond Lusshe—while same-day double cousin baptisms and shared burials prove the Melbury Abbas and Compton Abbas Lushes were one tight-knit family.
event.note: [DHC AD/DT/W/1673/30, Feb. 25, 1672/73] Will of John Lush of Melbury Abbas, yoman: £50 to dau. Elizabeth; £5 to son John [1707/09 testator]; residue to son Robert; overseers brothers-in-law Robert Burt of Haselbury & John Burden of Shaston. [DHC PE/COA/RE 1/1, Aug. 1676] Edmund LUSH, son of Nicholas & Mary [followed May 13, 1679 by same-day double baptism with John & Martha Lush].
Seeing Melbury Abbas Lush relatives ('Joseph LUSH, of Melbury Abbas' and widow Phillis/Philadelphia Lush) buried inside Compton Abbas churchyard proves both branches shared one family plot.

event.label: Dec. 10, 1677 – Nov. 16, 1703 — John Squire Marries Widow Anniver Roberts (1677), Elder Thomas Dies & Family Steps Into Alton Pancras (1678)
event.desc: Ten weeks after John Squire married Bookham neighbour widow Anniver Roberts, 76-year-old patriarch Thomas Squire senior died at Bookham (Feb. 1678). With the old three-lives lease ending on his death, John and Roger Squire moved 1.5 miles south across the hedge into Alton Pancras.
event.note: [DHC PE/BCN/RE 1/1, f. 157r] 10 Dec 1677: Joannes Squire de Sharnhull et Anniver Roberts vidua [widow of Guil. Roberts de Bockham senior, bur. 27 Sept 1672, f. 152v] — Nup | 21 Feb 1677/78: sepultus erat Thomas Squire de Bookham Senr — Sep | 15 Mar 1677/78: Rogerus filius Rogeri Ffarwell de [Bookham] eadem — Sep | f. 158v (3 Apr 1678): Gulielmus Holland — sep. [Alton Pancras PR] 16 Nov 1703: John Squire Senr — Buryed; 19 Feb 1710/11: Roger Squire — Buryed.
Reading the original ink on Frame 157r corrects an old index typo ('Anamer') back to 'Anniver Roberts', and confirms every Squire left Buckland Newton in Spring 1678.

event.label: Apr. 14, 1707 – Dec. 30, 1725 — Edmund Lush Marries Mary Lawrence (1707); Son Robert Marries by Licence on Christmas Eve 1718 & Signs Property Bond
event.desc: After Edmund Lush remarried to Somerset's Mary Lawrence, his eldest son Robert Lush paid for a marriage licence to wed Elizabeth Andrus (Andrews) in Shaftesbury on Christmas Eve 1718, signed a 1719/20 property settlement bond with his father Edmund, and baptized son Thomas Lush in Ashmore in 1725.
event.note: [PE/COA/RE 1/1, Apr. 14, 1707] Edmund Lush & Mary Lawrence [bapt. Oct. 22, 1690, Merriott]. [Holy Trinity Shaftesbury PR, Dec. 24, 1718] Robrt Lush Elizabeth Andrus dec 24 Licans. [DHC PE/LYD/MI 1, 1719/20] Covenant bond: Edmund Lush of Okeford Fitzpaine & eldest son Robert Lush 'of Sturminster Newton'. [Ashmore PR, Dec. 30, 1725] Thomas Lush christened.
Zooming into the cramped 1718 Shaftesbury handwriting proves the bride's surname was 'Andrus' (Andrews), fixing an old misreading of 'divrys'.

event.label: Dec. 24, 1709 – Mar. 14, 1732/33 — The Signature "John–Philip–Eleanor" Name Trio in Alton Pancras & Young Widower Philip Squire in Piddletrenthide
event.desc: John Squire Junr. and wife Eleanor introduce the distinctive name trio John, Philip, and Eleanor. Moving 1.5 miles east to Piddletrenthide, 23-year-old Philip Squire tragically lost his baby daughter Margaret and wife Mary within three weeks in early 1733, surviving with his young son John Squire.
event.note: [Alton Pancras PR, p. 18, Dec. 24, 1709] Philip ye son of John Squire & of Elea- / nor his wife — Bapt [Vicar John Wilcock] | [Feb. 8, 1729/30] Elnar the Wife [of John] Squier was bered | [Apr. 29, 1730] Squires John Holland bap. [Piddletrenthide PR, 1732/33, Vicar Jenkin Williams] Febry ye 23: Margaret Daughter of Philip Squire bury[ed]; March ye 14: Mary Wife of Phillip Squire was bury[ed].
We checked every 1700s Dorset record for 'Philip Squire' and ruled out a 1794 Royal Navy will that turned out to belong to a sailor named Philip Sparks.

event.label: 1745 – April 2, 1769 — Abraham Akerman Baptized in Broadwindsor (1745) & Pioneer Simon Squire Baptized in Chideock (April 2, 1769)
event.desc: Brings both Volume I lines to the West Dorset coast: Abraham Akerman is baptized at Broadwindsor in 1745 (6 miles from Bridport's rope and fishing-net walks), while John & Elizabeth Squire pass on the signature Alton Pancras names Philip, John, and Eleanor in seaside Chideock and baptize Newfoundland pioneer Simon Squire on April 2, 1769.
event.note: [Broadwindsor PR, 1745] Abraham, son of Daniel & Jean Akerman. [Whitchurch Canonicorum PR, June 5, 1750] Clement Furser & Eleanor Squire. [St. Giles Chideock PR, PE-CDK/RE/1/2, Apr. 2, 1769] Simon, son of John & Elisabeth Squire [with siblings Philip 1757, John 1759, Eleanor 1767; siblings William 1776 & Betty 1784 m. Farwell].
Original Chideock pages (ff. 36v–37r) prove a Nov. 2, 1777 'John Squire' burial was a 6-day-old baby grandson—confirming elder John Squire survived into the 1800s.

event.label: Jan. 17, 1773 – Jan. 22, 1795 — David Goulding Baptized in Wimborne (1773) & Pioneer John Lush Baptized in Motcombe (April 30, 1775)
event.desc: Pinpoints the exact Dorset baptisms of Greenspond pioneers David Goulding (Wimborne, 1773) and John Lush (Motcombe, April 30, 1775) before West Country fishing merchants recruited them across the Atlantic to Bonavista Bay.
event.note: [Wimborne Minster PR, Jan. 17, 1773] David Goulding bap. [St. Mary's Motcombe PR, 1753–1812] 19-Mar 1775: Ann Blandford dau. of William Blandford | 30-Apr 1775: John Lush son of John Lush was baptized. [Bower Chalke Will of John Newman, proved Jan. 22, 1795] £120 to 'my sisters son John Lush, now living in the parish of Motcomb'.

Solves a famous mistake on internet family trees that claimed John Lush was born in 'Blandford Forum'—right above John Lush's line on the 1775 Motcombe page is a baby named 'Ann Blandford', whose last name was misread as a town! Because Motcombe's clerk omitted mothers' names before 1777, two local Blackmore Vale kinsmen remain open as the father 'John Lush': John Lush (bapt. 1757, Melbury Abbas) or an older Newman-linked kinsman named in the 1795 Bower Chalke will.

event.label: c. 1780–1815 — Founding of Emure Ijaloke (Nigeria): Ancestral Osukoti Seat (Idamudu) & High Chief Ojomu Arintokun (Odo-Emure)
event.desc: When the Yorùbá kingdom of Emure moved from Igbo-Owa to its permanent capital at Emure Ijaloke around 1780, our paternal ancestors established the hereditary Osukoti quarter-chieftaincy in Idamudu while maternal ancestors under High Chief Ojomu Arintokun anchored the senior kingmaker house in Odo-Emure.
event.note: [Emure Royal Chronicles, r. Oba Adumori Ogunragaboja c. 1780–1845 & INEC Land Directory] Ward 07 Idamudu I (13/06/07/003): At Osunkoti [Ilé Ọ̀ṣùnkọ́tì]. Ward 04 Odo-Emure IV (13/06/04/002): Ojumu Akeregun [High Chief Ojomu Arintokun, senior Ìwàrẹ̀fà kingmaker].
Official ward and polling maps keep Odo-Emure's senior kingmaker title 'Ojomu / Ojumu' strictly separate from a different 'Ojimo' title in Oke-Emure.

event.label: 1792 – August 18, 1798 — Lay Minister "A Ackerman" Officiates His Daughter Jane's 1798 Wedding to Simon Squires in Bonavista, NL
event.desc: Unites the Chideock Squire and Broadwindsor Akerman families in Newfoundland: because Bonavista had no ordained priest, Jane's educated father Abraham Akerman Sr. served for 30+ years as lay minister and personally married Jane to Simon Squires Sr. on August 18, 1798.
event.note: [USPG C/CAN/NFL: 2, Nov. 20, 1792] Magistrate John Bland recommends stipend for 'Abraham Akerman for officiating as minister, or catechist'. [PANL Bonavista C of E Marriage PR, Feb. 17 & Aug. 18, 1798] Andrew Pearce & Hannah Ackerman; Simon Squires & Jane Akerman — By Whom Married: A Ackerman.
Original missionary letters at Oxford (USPG C/CAN/NFL: 2) and Bonavista marriage entries independently verify Abraham Akerman Sr.'s clerical role and handwritten signature.

event.label: 1802 — 72-Year-Old John Squire Leases Cottage "Lushes" Beside St. Giles Church in Chideock, Dorset
event.desc: Four years after his son Simon Squire married in Bonavista, 72-year-old John Squire was still living next door to St. Giles Church in Chideock on a cottage plot remarkably named 'Lushes'—foreshadowing Pleman Squires and Ivy Lush's Newfoundland wedding 142 years later and fixing John's birth to c. 1729/30!
event.note: [DHC Ref: D-WLC, 1802 Manor of Chideock Sale Particulars & Leasehold Survey, Arundell to Weld] Tenement 'Lushes' adjoining St. Giles Church & George Webber at The George Inn: John Squire, aged 72 [born c. 1729/30], holding 99-year lease determinable on three lives at 2s. 6d. yearly rent.
Because Mary Squire died in Piddletrenthide in March 1732/33, John's exact age of 72 in 1802 places his birth squarely inside Philip and Mary Squire's marriage window.

event.label: Jan. 14, 1817 – April 19, 1851 — Bonavista Pioneers Laid to Rest & Abraham Akerman Jr.'s "Blue Cloth Jacket" Will (1843/44)
event.desc: Captures the full arc of our first Newfoundland generation in Bonavista: lay minister Abraham Akerman Sr. baptizing his grandchildren into his seventies before dying in 1822 (aged 77), pioneer Simon Squires Sr. dying in 1832 (aged 63), uncle Abraham Akerman Jr. leaving his prized blue cloth jacket to his Squires great-nephew in 1843/44, and matriarch Jane Akerman Squires living to 1851 (aged 78).
event.note: [PANL Bonavista PRs] Jan. 14, 1817: Jane dau. of Simon & Jane Squire — Bapt. by A. Ackerman | 1822 Burial: ABRAHAM AKERMAN, age 77 | 1832 Burial: Simon Squires, age 63 | Apr. 19, 1851 Burial: Jane Squires, age 78. [NL Will Books Vol. 1, p. 455, Dec. 26, 1843 / 1844] Will of Abraham Akerman Jr.: bequeaths blue cloth jacket to '...... Squires, son of John Squires'.
Every Bonavista burial age (77 in 1822 = 1745; 63 in 1832 = 1769) matches the family's English parish baptisms in Broadwindsor and Chideock to the exact year.

event.label: 1826 – May 26, 1840 & 1857 — Greenspond Granite Island Pioneers, Thomas Lush & Mary Goulding Wedding (1840) & Church Timber Haul
event.desc: On rocky, windswept Greenspond Island—so barren of soil that families hauled boatloads of earth from the mainland just to plant a vegetable garden—Thomas Lush married Mary Goulding on May 26, 1840, uniting two Dorset pioneer families in Bonavista Bay.
event.note: [Greenspond Community & Parish Records] Dorset pioneers David Goulding (1773–1826, Fryer & Fryer recruit) & John Lush (1775–1827; widow Elizabeth Jane Wood, 1777–1847) | May 26, 1840 Marriage: Thomas Lush (c. 1812–1887) & Mary Goulding (1821–1869, dau. of Jacob Goulding, who hauled timber in 1857 for St. Stephen's Church).
Verified directly through Greenspond parish registers and St. Stephen's parish building records.

event.label: 1846 – c. 1856 — Irish Methodist Crossing: Fethard Schoolmaster Philip Dwyer (1846) & Twillingate Dwyer–Thorne Marriage
event.desc: Follows our Irish-Newfoundland branch across the Atlantic: departing via the Waterford–Twillingate trade route, Irish Methodist fisherman and captain John Alexander Dwyer married Hillview-born Caroline Bemister Thorne around 1856—carrying forward the rare Protestant Tipperary names Philip and Alexander seen in 1846 Fethard schoolmaster Philip Dwyer.
event.note: [1846 Fethard Directory, Co. Tipperary] Philip Dwyer, Master of Parochial School, Chapel Lane [Working Lead]. [Hillview & Twillingate Records, c. 1856] Marriage of Irish Methodist pioneer Capt. John Alexander Dwyer (c. 1830–Jan. 6, 1907) & Caroline Bemister Thorne (c. 1837–Nov. 4, 1906, born Hillview, Trinity Bay to Richard Thorne of Exford, Somerset & Betsy George).
John Alexander Dwyer's Methodist faith and Philip/Alexander naming pattern stand out sharply in Tipperary, giving researchers clear targets in Dublin vestry minutes and Slade & Co. ledgers.

event.label: 1836 – September 2, 1862 — Squires Push North: Herring Neck Foothold (1836 Census) & Silas Squires's 1862 Nipper's Harbour Wedding
event.desc: As Bonavista's fishing rooms grew crowded, Simon and Julia Squires pushed north into Notre Dame Bay at Herring Neck by 1836, and their son Silas Squires married Sarah Jane Noble at Nipper's Harbour on September 2, 1862 before settling permanently in Smiths Harbour.
event.note: [1836 NL Colonial Census, Twillingate & Fogo — Herring Neck] Simon Squires [Jr., b. c. 1814/15, & wife Julia], alongside John & Thomas Squires. [Nipper's Harbour Methodist/C of E Register, Sept. 2, 1862] Marriage of Silas Squires (c. 1841–1903) & Sarah Jane Noble (1844–1901), founding the Smiths Harbour Squires household.
Anchored by the 1836 nominal colonial census and the surviving 1862 Nipper's Harbour marriage entry.

event.label: 1871 – 1878 — Why Our Pioneers Left England: 78-Year-Old Cousin George Lush Listed as a "Pauper" in Motcombe (1871)
event.desc: Provides a vivid human window into why John Lush and Simon Squire braved the North Atlantic: back in Motcombe, Dorset, after the Enclosure Acts fenced off common pastures and wiped out small yeoman copyholders, 78-year-old cousin George Lush ended his days listed as a parish 'Pauper' in 1871.
event.note: [1871 UK Census, Motcombe, Dorset — 'North End'] George Lush (1793–1878, aged 78, stay-behind Dorset collateral branch, brother of Hannah & Mary Doggrell) — Occupation/Condition: 'Pauper'.
Cross-checked against Motcombe burial records (d. 1878) and Blackmore Vale Doggrell marriage registers.

event.label: c. 1850 – c. 1880 — Patriarch Kọ́ládé on the River Ose, Royal Owo–Emure Marriage & Life-Sized Carved Àkó Effigy (c. 1880)
event.desc: Shows how Generation 5 patriarch Kọ́ládé's personal given name became our permanent family surname Kolade, while 22 km east in Owo, royal ruler High Chief Ojomo Agunloye I (whose death c. 1880 is dated by his famous life-sized carved wooden effigy) allied his house with Emure's Ojomu kingmakers through his daughter Olajenboye.
event.note: [Yorùbá Name History & Gazetteer #35] [Ògún]kọ́ládé ('He who gathers honour and arrives') + son Ògúnlúsì ('Ogun possesses renown') at Oko Ọ̀sẹ Kọ́ládé. [Abiodun 1976, Africa 46.1 & Emure Chronicles] Carved wooden àkó burial effigy of High Chief Ojomo Agunloye I of Ijebu-Owo (d. c. 1880), father of Olajenboye (married High Chief Ojomu Ogedu of Emure).
Carefully distinguishes Owo's royal ruler ('Ojomo Oluda') from Emure's senior kingmaker ('Ojomu of Odo-Emure') and maps out three ways Ojomu Ogedu connects to Lydia Olugbe's father.

event.label: 1874 – September 1886 — Kiriji Peace Treaty (Sept. 1886): Chief Daniel Ogunlusi Kolade & Alice Awawu Plant Christianity in Emure-Ekiti
event.desc: Immediately after the September 1886 Kiriji Peace Treaty ended nine years of regional war, quarter-chief Daniel Ogunlusi Kolade (The Osukoti) and merchant-banker Alice Awawu Kolade returned to Idamudu Quarter to help found Emure-Ekiti's pioneer Christian community—while Alice's commercial credit loans became famous in a local town proverb.
event.note: [St. Paul's Emure Memorials 1989, 1996 p. 10 & J.A. p. 15] Following the Ibadan–Emure (1874–75) & Kiriji Wars (Sept. 1886, ni kete ti ogun Kiriji pari): Chief Daniel Ogunlusi Kolade (The Osukoti of Emure-Ekiti), Madam Alice Awawu Kolade & Madam Sarah Fafunbo Kolade ('onisowo ekini'). Proverb: 'Èmi kò ní dá ẹlẹ́ṣinrin (gbèsè) Àwáwù, kí n di ẹrú Marian!'
Independently attested across five printed St. Paul's Anglican funeral programmes and INEC compound coordinates (13/06/08/004).

event.label: 1883 – January 6, 1907 — Tilt Cove Copper Boom, Birth of Rev. Philip H. Lush (1888), 1895 Mine Tragedy, Lushes Bight & Burlington
event.desc: Captures our family's rugged copper-mining chapter on the sheer cliffs of Tilt Cove—where William Lush and Polly Dwyer raised their young family (including future Maine minister Rev. Philip H. Lush) and mourned Polly's 25-year-old miner brother Albert Dwyer in 1895—before establishing Lushes Bight and settling in Burlington / North West Arm.
event.note: [Tilt Cove, Twillingate Sun & Death Reg. Bk 5] 1883 m. William Lush (1845–1922) & Mary Ann 'Polly' Dwyer (1863–Aug. 27, 1905) | Oct. 11, 1888 Tilt Cove birth of Rev. Philip Henry Lush (1888–1967, ordained in Portland & Kennebunkport, Maine; siblings Caroline, William George, Alexander Dwyer, James Edward, WWI vet Stanley & Albert) | Dec. 4, 1895 Tilt Cove mining death of Albert Edward Dwyer (age 25) | Nov. 4, 1906 & Jan. 6, 1907 deaths of Caroline & Capt. John A. Dwyer.
Cross-checked across Tilt Cove birth records, the Dec. 1895 Twillingate Sun, New England ministry records, and Twillingate Death Register Book 5.

event.label: 1913 – 1935 — First Ontario Foothold in Sudbury (1913) & Smiths Harbour Sawmill / Medical Boat Pioneers
event.desc: Marks both the family's earliest mainland bridge to Ontario—cousin William Silas Squires marrying in the rail-and-mining hub of Sudbury in 1913—and the community backbone of Smiths Harbour, where William & Mary-Jane Squires and sawmill/medical-boat pioneer Albert & Florence Lush raised Pleman Squires, Ivy Lush, and Daisy Lush Rideout.
event.note: [Archives of Ontario Marriage Reg., 1913, Sudbury] William Silas Squires (nephew of William Squires) & Ethel Jane Brown. [NL Nominal Censuses 1921, 1935 & 1945, Smiths Harbour] William Squires (b. 1865) & Mary-Jane Budgell (b. 1879); Albert Lush (1898–1980) & Florence White (operating steam sawmill & medical boat; daughters Ivy Lush, bapt. Nov. 7, 1921, & Daisy Evelyn Lush, 1922–2007, m. Rubert Rideout).
Verified across Ontario civil marriage registers, three Newfoundland censuses (1921–1945), and Smiths Harbour cemetery headstones.

event.label: 1919 – 1933 — Prime Minister (Olisa) Alliance, St. Paul's School (1919) & Kolade Brothers Enter C.M.S. Bookshops (1922 & 1933)
event.desc: Shows Generation 3 turning merchant capital into educational and civic leadership across colonial Nigeria: eldest sister Serra-Ann Marian married Emure's Prime Minister (The Olisa), elder half-brother John Aderibigbe joined C.M.S. Bookshops in Benin City in 1922 and trained as a nurse in Ibadan, and Pa Joseph Owolabi Kolade ('Baba Bookseller') launched his 25-year C.M.S. Bookshops career in 1933.
event.note: [Oke Memorial 1996 p. 10, J.A. Kolade p. 15 & J.O. Kolade 1989] Serra-Ann Marian Kolade (c. 1891–1996) m. Chief Benjamin Oke Apata, The Olisa [Prime Minister] of Emure-Ekiti | 1919: St. Paul's C.M.S. School founded | Chief John Aderibigbe Kolade (b. May 13, 1905; fostered by Chief Adefemi, The Sasere; CMS Bookshops Benin City 1922; Adeoyo Hospital nursing, Ibadan) | Pa Joseph Owolabi Kolade ('Baba Bookseller', b. Oct. 27, 1907; St. Paul's Emure & St. Patrick's Owo; joined CMS Bookshops Benin City 1933).
Cross-verified across three independent St. Paul's Emure funeral biographies and colonial mission school milestones.

event.label: 1942 – September 6, 1944 — Two Wartime Weddings: Joseph Kolade & Lydia Olugbe (1942 Nigeria) and Pleman Squires & Ivy Lush (Sept. 6, 1944 NL)
event.desc: Just two years apart during World War II, Pa Joseph Kolade and Madam Lydia Olugbe united the Osukoti and Ojomu houses in Benin City (welcoming Victor Olusoji Kolade in 1942), while Pleman Squires and Ivy Lush united the Squires–Akerman and Lush–Lawrence–Goulding–Dwyer lines in Smiths Harbour (welcoming Merle Elizabeth Squires in December 1944).
event.note: [L. O. Kolade Memorial 2010] 1942 Benin City marriage: Pa Joseph Owolabi Kolade & Madam Lydia Olugbe Kolade ('Mama Dudu', c. 1918–May 28, 2010, dau. of Late Chief Ojomu of Odo-Emure); birth of Victor Olusoji Kolade (July 30, 1942). [Smiths Harbour Register, Sept. 6, 1944] Marriage of Pleman Squires (b. 1911) & Ivy Lush (bapt. Nov. 7, 1921); birth of Merle Elizabeth Squires (Dec. 31, 1944).
Verified directly from Newfoundland United Church and civil records alongside Nigerian Anglican memorials.

event.label: October 1947 – 1958 — Ondo & Ado-Ekiti Years: Canon Awosika's 1947 Baptism, "Mama Dudu's" Wholesale Bakery & CMS Conferences
event.desc: Chronicles a vibrant decade of entrepreneurship and education across Ondo, Ado-Ekiti, and Ibadan: while 'Baba Bookseller' reorganized C.M.S. Bookshops branches and addressed conferences in Lagos and Ibadan, 'Mama Dudu' built an independent catering and wholesale baking distribution network between Ado-Ekiti and Emure-Ekiti.
event.note: [St. Stephen's Oke-Aluko, Ondo PR, Oct. 1947 & E.B. Kolade p. 14] Canon S. O. Awosika baptizes Eric [Edward] Christian Jones Bamidele Kolade (son of Pa Joseph & senior wife Victoria Wuraola; Ibadan Grammar School, Headmaster & Ibadan YMCA co-founder). [J.O. & L.O. Kolade Memorials] Ondo (1946–54) & Ado-Ekiti (1954–58) CMS Bookshops reorganization; Mama Dudu supplies ẹ̀kọ to Ondo Teacher Training College & runs Ado–Emure wholesale bread/cake network while raising Victor Olusoji, Theophilus Olaniran & Henry Olatunji Kolade.
Anchored by the October 1947 St. Stephen's Ondo baptism entry and three independent family memorial biographies.

event.label: 1960 – 1968 — Emure Customary Court Presidency (1960–63) & Installation of Chief John A. Kolade as The Osukoti (1968)
event.desc: Marks the modern civic restoration of our paternal Idamudu chieftaincy seat: at Nigerian Independence in 1960, elder uncle Chief John Aderibigbe Kolade presided over the Emure-Ekiti Customary Court before being formally installed in 1968 as The Osukoti of Emure-Ekiti.
event.note: [J. A. Kolade Memorial, p. 15 & INEC 13/06/07/003] Chief John Aderibigbe Kolade (b. May 13, 1905): President of Emure-Ekiti Customary Court (1960–1963) at Nigerian Independence; formally installed in 1968 in the hereditary Idamudu chieftaincy title of The Osukoti of Emure-Ekiti previously held by his father Chief Daniel Ogunlusi Kolade.
Cross-checked between the post-1968 Osukoti biography and Idamudu I Ward cadastral unit 13/06/07/003 ('At Osunkoti').

event.label: December 1966 – c. 1970 — Victor Olusoji Kolade Arrives in Canada (Dec. 1966), Serves in the Canadian Armed Forces & Settles in Toronto
event.desc: Traces the remarkable transatlantic journey that brought our Nigerian and Newfoundland worlds together: arriving in Victoria, B.C. in December 1966 and serving in the Canadian Armed Forces out of CFB Shilo, Manitoba, Victor Olusoji Kolade first connected with Merle Elizabeth Squires in Newfoundland as pen pals before moving to Toronto around 1969–1970 after his honourable discharge.
event.note: [Canadian Service & Family Biographical Archive] Dec. 1966: Victor Olusoji Kolade (b. July 30, 1942, eldest son of Pa Joseph & Madam Lydia Kolade) immigrates to Victoria, B.C.; 1967: enlists in the Canadian Armed Forces (stationed at CFB Shilo, Manitoba), meeting Merle Elizabeth Squires of Smiths Harbour, NL via a newspaper pen-pals column; c. 1969–1970: moves to Toronto, Ontario following his honourable discharge to further his education.
Preserved directly in Victor Olusoji Kolade's family eulogy and Canadian civil/service records.

event.label: 1973 — 1973 Marriage of Victor Olusoji Kolade & Merle Elizabeth Squires — Uniting Nigeria & Newfoundland in Toronto
event.desc: Dedicated Generation 2 milestone: in 1973, Victor Olusoji Kolade and Merle Elizabeth Squires married—uniting 15 generations of Dorset, Somerset, Irish, and Newfoundland outport pioneers with 5 generations of Emure-Ekiti and Owo chieftaincy and C.M.S. leaders, and establishing our modern family home in Toronto, Ontario.
event.note: [Canadian Civil & Family Records, 1973] Marriage of Victor Olusoji Kolade (July 30, 1942 – Aug. 31, 2017; brothers Theophilus Olaniran, Henry Olatunji & half-brother Eric Bamidele Kolade) and Merle Elizabeth Squires (Dec. 31, 1944 – Aug. 17, 2025; first cousins Palma Squires, Paul Knight, and Jerry, Shirley, Bernice & Dereck Rideout), building their 36-year working life and musical home in Toronto, Ontario.
Anchored by Canadian marriage and death certificates, Nigerian memorial programmes, and the Pine Hills Cemetery family monument.

event.label: November 1989 – May 28, 2010 — Primate Dr. T. O. Olufosoye Preaches Pa Joseph Kolade's 1989 Funeral & Passing of Emure Matriarchs (1996 & 2010)
event.desc: Honours the closing chapter of Generation 3 in Emure-Ekiti: when 'Baba Bookseller' died at age 81 in 1989, the retired First Archbishop and Primate of All Nigeria personally traveled to St. Paul's Emure-Ekiti to preach his funeral sermon, followed by the centenarian life of Aunt Serra-Ann Oke (1996) and grandmother 'Mama Dudu' (2010).
event.note: [St. Paul's Anglican Church, Emure-Ekiti Memorials] Nov. 1989: Funeral of Pa Joseph Owolabi Kolade ('Baba Bookseller', Oct. 27, 1907 – Oct. 10, 1989), sermon preached by The Most Revd. Dr. Timothy Omotayo Olufosoye (Rtd.), First Archbishop & Primate of the Church of Nigeria | Feb. 3, 1996: Passing of eldest sister Madam Serra-Ann Marian Oke (c. 1891–1996) | May 28, 2010: Passing of matriarch Madam Lydia Olugbe Kolade ('Mama Dudu', c. 1918–2010).
Documented verbatim on the printed 1989, 1996, and 2010 St. Paul's Anglican liturgical programmes.

event.label: August 2017 – 2026 — Scarborough Charcoal Granite Monument (Pine Hills Lot 2436H) & Living Generation 1 Synthesis in Toronto
event.desc: Inscribes our transatlantic convergence in permanent stone at Pine Hills Cemetery in Scarborough—explicitly naming both Emure-Ekiti, Nigeria and Smith's Harbour, Newfoundland—while Victor Olutayo Kolade and Abigail Salole carry 551 years of verified family history forward in Toronto.
event.note: [Pine Hills Cemetery, Scarborough, Section A, Lot 2436H, 2026 Charcoal Granite Monument] KOLADE — Victor Olusoji of Emure-Ekiti, Nigeria (1942–2017) & Merle Elizabeth (née Squires) of Smith's Harbour, NL (1944–2025). [Toronto, ON] Victor Olutayo Kolade & Abigail Salole [Living — Generation 1].
Living birth dates and neighbourhood details are kept private in this public-safe edition.
